coachMessages.text: Five discs up the centre, then four up the next column over — the '5-4' opening. Gray, to move here, is already lost.

slides.infoProse: This is Allen's flagship central-column win: Green stacks the centre column five discs high, then continues into the neighbouring column, always blocking Gray's horizontal ideas as it goes. Once the shape is complete, Green already holds a winning odd-row threat on the far side — Gray, to move, has no defence.

coachMessages.text: Green grabbed both central key cells early — the third and fourth cells of the centre column. This D3-D4 opening is usually an easy win, but here it has sharpened: Green to move, and only ONE column wins.

slides.infoProse: Owning both central key cells early — Allen's D3 and D4 — is usually powerful and comparatively easy to convert. But 'usually easy' does not mean 'always safe': in this exact position, only the second column from the left keeps the win — every other column throws it away. Recognising the D3-D4 shape tells you the position is good; it does not tell you which move keeps it that way.

coachMessages.text: Same centre column, but Gray never let Green claim that second central cell. Gray, to move here, still loses — but the win is thinner than the D3-D4 lines.

slides.infoProse: This is the sibling '3-4' opening: Green's centre column stands only three high (no D4), so the easy D3-D4 plan is unavailable and Green's win depends on a delayed, more precise follow-up instead. It is still a Green win here, but a thin one — and a self-trapping one: Allen notes that once the centre is left at three high, a LATER D4 by Green often turns into the blunder that throws the win away.

socratic.goalPrompt: Green dominates the third row on the right, Gray has compensation on the fifth row on the left. Green to move — only one column wins. Which one?
socratic._boardInstructions: 16 plies (3265533353553111): a Third-Row Gambit — Green (first player) has a major third-row threat on the right flank (cols 4-6), Gray has fifth-row compensation on the left flank (cols 1-2). Green (first player) to move. No overlays: nothing should hint at the answer before the student attempts it. Solver-verified (Allen Diagram 301): col 4 (0-indexed) is the unique positive-scoring column (+2); every other playable column is negative for Green.

ask.text: Green dominates the third row on the right, Gray has compensation on the fifth row on the left. Green to move — only one column wins. Which one?
ask.text_es: Verde domina la tercera fila a la derecha, Gris tiene compensación en la quinta fila a la izquierda. Verde mueve — solo una columna gana. ¿Cuál es?

wrong1.text: Not quite — look for the right square. Try again.
wrong1.text_es: No exactamente — buscá la casilla correcta. Intentalo de nuevo.

correct.text: Exactly — that column completes Green's third-row threat right now. Every other column throws the win away; this is Allen's 'only one move to win' Third-Row Gambit.
correct.text_es: Exacto — esa columna completa la amenaza de tercera fila de Verde ahora mismo. Cualquier otra columna desperdicia la victoria; este es el 'Third-Row Gambit' de Allen, la única jugada que gana.

hint.text: Look at Green's threats on the right flank. Which column completes them right now?
hint.text_es: Mirá las amenazas de Verde en el flanco derecho. ¿Qué columna las completa ahora mismo?
